item.title: In a Sky Ruled by Ancient Birds, Bats Conquered the Dark
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: National Audubon Society.
Summary: A starlit forest rustles in the dark. Ancient birds sleep beneath a Cenozoic moon, survivors from the age of dinosaurs just recently passed. In the velvet gloom, a small, shrew-like mammal swings on...

item.title: A train was delayed by a solar storm. But something didn't add up.
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: ScienceDaily.
Summary: Scientists have cracked a 178-year-old mystery surrounding a train delayed by a solar storm, revealing that the famous incident happened in 1848 rather than 1841. The discovery rewrites the early history of space weather and highlights a threat that still endangers modern power grids, satellites, and communication systems.
Waypoint’s Take: Outside, this matters because it can change what you watch for: compare forecast cues with what the sky, wind, and ground feel like before you commit to a route. Keep the publisher’s claims provisional until you read the original. If you go out, pair the story with current Dashboard readings rather than the headline alone.
